Cautiously constructive tone. The FOMC holds a restrictive stance (5.25–5.50% target range) while noting “further progress” toward 2% and “better balance” of risks. In standard policy-rule terms (Taylor rule; Clarida, Galí, and Gertler), inflation still above target and only a modest rise in unemployment justify keeping policy tight until confidence about disinflation is higher. The emphasis on “greater confidence” and data dependence aligns with optimal inflation-targeting/expectations management (Svensson and Woodford) and supports gradualism under uncertainty (Söderström; Wieland). Continued balance-sheet runoff and corridor implementation (IOER, ON RRP) are consistent with post-2008 operating frameworks. Net effect: positive on growth and disinflation progress, tempered by a firm commitment to restraint until inflation is sustainably at target.
